items.title: Anticipatory RL for Non-Markovian Jump-Diffusion Markets
items.source_summary: Paper introduces Anticipatory Reinforcement Learning framework using signature-augmented state spaces to capture path-dependent geometry in jump-diffusion environments with structural breaks. Proposes self-consistent field approach to maintain history as dynamical coordinates, addressing failures of classical state-based methods under single-trajectory constraints.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's prediction pipeline (AI synthesis, scoring methodology) currently relies on Markovian assumptions in feature engineering and state representation. The GEX calculator and options flow detection assume stationary regimes; they do not model path-dependent effects or structural breaks dynamically. Signature methods and lifted state spaces could enhance regime detection in `vix_term_structure.py`, `gex_calculator.py`, and the feature engineering layer (`data_preprocessing.py`). Jump-diffusion handling is absent in delta-hedging flow inference.

proposed_change.change_description: Integrate signature-space lifting for path-dependent feature construction. Replace static state snapshots with signature augmentation capturing cumulative return geometry. Apply self-consistent field approach to regime classification in structural break detection. Test on jump-diffusion synthetic markets (Merton-style jumps) before live deployment.

items.evidence_basis: Signature methods are mathematically rigorous but abstract; no empirical comparison vs. existing RL approaches on real volatility data provided. Relevance hinges on whether SOFAR encounters frequent structural breaks/jumps (likely in tail events).
items.credibility_basis: arXiv preprint from quantitative finance subfield; signature-based state lifting is established in applied ML.
items.author: Daniel Bloch

items.title: α-Robust Utility Maximization for Ambiguous Claim Dependencies
items.source_summary: Paper addresses portfolio optimization under ambiguity about dependence structure between contingent claims and market returns. Uses α-robust criterion interpolating worst- and best-case scenarios; proves risk measure is law-invariant under exponential utilities, reducing dynamic control to static optimization via quantile methods.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's risk management and position-sizing logic (if present) likely assumes known market correlations and claim dependencies. This paper reveals a blind spot: SOFAR does not explicitly model ambiguity about tail dependence or basis risk in synthetic payoffs (e.g., OTC options flows vs. spot). The alpha-robust framework could enhance `risk_management.py` and `position_sizer.py` by parameterizing ambiguity attitudes (α). Quantile optimization could replace or augment current utility assumptions.

proposed_change.change_description: Introduce α-robust utility framework with configurable ambiguity parameter. Implement law-invariant risk measure using quantile optimization for synthetic options positions. Model dependence uncertainty between derivatives flows and underlying spot returns. Backtest position sizing under varying α (0=worst-case, 1=best-case).

items.evidence_basis: Mathematical proof provided for law-invariance under weighted exponential utilities. Real-world applicability depends on whether SOFAR's claim universe includes OTC derivatives with sparse dependence data.
items.credibility_basis: arXiv quantitative finance; rearrangement inequalities and comonotonicity are classical techniques.
items.author: Xinyu Chen, Zuo Quan Xu

items.title: Co-Pricing Factor Zoo: Equity-Bond Factor Redundancy & SDF Density
items.source_summary: Paper analyzes 18 quadrillion asset pricing models jointly for corporate bonds and equities, finding equity and nontradable factors suffice to explain bond risk premia after accounting for Treasury term structure. Concludes true latent SDF is dense in observable factor space; Bayesian Model Averaging SDF outperforms low-dimensional alternatives in- and out-of-sample.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's AI synthesis and scoring methodology likely uses a fixed or small set of volatility/flow factors for prediction. The paper reveals that a single parsimonious factor set is suboptimal; the true pricing kernel is distributed across many factors. SOFAR's `ai_synthesis.py` and factor selection logic (`feature_importance.py`, `model_selection.py`) should employ Bayesian Model Averaging rather than univariate factor ranking or hard selection. This impacts GEX decomposition and options flow weighting.

proposed_change.change_description: Replace hard factor selection with Bayesian Model Averaging over all candidate signals (GEX components, VIX term structure, options flow skew, sentiment, macro). Weight factor contributions by marginal likelihoods; ensemble SDF across equity-bond-vol triplet. Validate on out-of-sample bond-equity-volatility triple pricing.

items.evidence_basis: 18 quadrillion model enumeration is empirically rigorous; out-of-sample superiority of BMA-SDF is quantified. Directly addresses model selection under uncertainty.
items.credibility_basis: arXiv; large-scale computational factor analysis with cross-asset (equity-bond) validation.
items.author: Alexander Dickerson, Christian Julliard, Philippe Mueller

items.title: Forecasting Tangency Portfolios via Efficient Frontier Decomposition
items.source_summary: Paper proposes two-stage model: first forecasts tangency portfolio by decomposing efficient frontier functional form (square-root second-order polynomial) into three interpretable coefficients using VAR; second stage uses this to select optimal portfolio. Demonstrates superior out-of-sample Sharpe ratios.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's `position_sizer.py` or portfolio construction likely uses static tangency portfolio or empirical mean-variance optimization. This paper shows tangency portfolio (optimal risk-adjusted return boundary) is predictable via time-series decomposition of efficient frontier coefficients. SOFAR could enhance dynamic hedging and asset allocation by forecasting frontier shape shifts. Directly applicable to weighting of GEX signals, options flow indicators, and VIX components into hedge ratios.

proposed_change.change_description: Implement efficient frontier polynomial decomposition (3 coefficients). Forecast coefficients using VAR on rolling windows. Dynamically update tangency portfolio weights for options hedge ratios and GEX flow allocation. Backtest out-of-sample Sharpe vs. static allocation; measure transaction cost impact.

items.evidence_basis: Concrete algorithmic contribution with out-of-sample validation. VAR forecasting of frontier coefficients is parsimonious and testable.
items.credibility_basis: arXiv finance; mean-variance portfolio theory is foundational; efficient frontier decomposition is mathematically sound.
items.author: Nolan Alexander, William Scherer

items.title: Markov Regime Detection via Clustered Efficient Frontier Coefficients
items.source_summary: Paper proposes asset allocation using Markov processes where states are defined by clustered efficient frontier coefficients rather than return/volatility. Monthly hierarchical clustering of three frontier coefficients provides dimensionality reduction of return and covariance matrix, enabling regime-aware portfolio rebalancing.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's regime detection (if present in `vix_term_structure.py`, `gex_calculator.py`, or `feature_engineering.py`) likely relies on volatility levels, realized correlation, or hidden Markov models on returns. This paper reveals that efficient frontier geometry (not first/second moments alone) contains richer regime information. SOFAR could enhance structural break detection and regime-dependent GEX scaling by clustering frontier coefficients. Applicable to dynamic VIX term structure model selection.

proposed_change.change_description: Extract efficient frontier coefficients (square-root polynomial) from rolling window of asset returns. Apply hierarchical clustering monthly. Use cluster membership as discrete Markov state. Condition GEX calculations, VIX term structure model, and options flow weighting on regime state. Backtest regime transition prediction vs. realized vol breaks.

items.evidence_basis: Concrete Markov regime framework with hierarchical clustering; efficient frontier decomposition is mathematically tractable and implementable.
items.credibility_basis: arXiv finance; Markov regimes and frontier-based clustering are novel but well-motivated extension of existing regime-switching literature.
items.author: Nolan Alexander, William Scherer, Jamey Thompson

items.title: PolySwarm: Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Prediction Market Trading
items.source_summary: Paper presents PolySwarm, a multi-agent LLM framework deploying 50 diverse language model personas to evaluate binary outcome markets on decentralized platforms (Polymarket). Aggregates probability estimates via confidence-weighted Bayesian combination, applies information-theoretic analysis (KL/JS divergence), and uses quarter-Kelly sizing for risk control.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's AI synthesis methodology (`ai_synthesis.py`, `sentiment_analysis.py`, `scoring.py`) likely uses deterministic rules or single-model inference. PolySwarm reveals that ensemble diversity in LLM personas + information-theoretic divergence metrics (KL/JS) + confidence weighting + Kelly sizing yield superior real-time pricing predictions. SOFAR could enhance sentiment scoring and event tree construction by deploying multi-perspective LLM consensus with divergence-based confidence calibration. Applicable to binary event prediction (Fed rate, earnings surprises).

proposed_change.change_description: Deploy ensemble of 10-20 LLM personas (system prompts varied for hawkish/dovish/technical/macro perspectives) on event questions (e.g., 'Will FOMC raise rates?'). Aggregate via confidence-weighted Bayesian combination. Compute KL divergence vs. market-implied probabilities for surprise magnitude. Apply quarter-Kelly to probability mismatch. Validate on prediction markets (Manifold, Metaculus) before using in SOFAR's real-time scoring.

items.evidence_basis: PolySwarm framework is deployed on real decentralized markets but paper focuses on binary outcomes; applicability to continuous (options) pricing requires extension. Multi-agent LLM consensus is empirically validated on Polymarket.
items.credibility_basis: arXiv; practical deployment on Polymarket with real financial stakes; information-theoretic divergence metrics are standard.
items.author: Rajat M. Barot, Arjun S. Borkhatariya

items.title: Adaptive VaR Control for Standardized Option Books under Marking Frictions
items.source_summary: Framework for next-day Value-at-Risk forecasting in options portfolios using conditional quantile estimation and conformal recalibration to handle valuation frictions and tail-risk instability across changing market regimes.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's risk_management and backtesting modules lack explicit next-day VaR forecasting for standardized option books. Current pipeline (gex_calculator.py, options_flow_detector.py) focuses on intraday Greeks and flow detection but does not model tail-risk under marking frictions or adaptive recalibration. The prediction_backcheck.py does not include conformal prediction intervals calibrated to realized next-day losses, which is critical for capital allocation in derivatives desks.

proposed_change.change_description: Implement adaptive VaR module with sequential conformal recalibration: (1) base conditional quantile model on next-day realized losses for option books; (2) add marking friction adjustment layer for off-the-run contracts; (3) integrate into prediction_backcheck.py to evaluate forecast stability under regime shifts; (4) flag high-friction periods in signal synthesis when option flow confidence drops.
proposed_change.estimated_effort: 3-4 weeks (quantile model + conformal calibration + integration with backtester)

items.evidence_basis: Directly addresses standardized derivatives risk, next-day realization challenges, and tail-risk instability—core pain points for option traders. Conformal prediction is well-validated methodology.
items.credibility_basis: arXiv quantitative finance, focuses on practical next-day frictions, testable on real option data.
items.author: Tenghan Zhong
